title: Kirak tool declarations
description: The "tools" map of a Kirak config file that offers tools to a model (MCP server files; agent files). Each key is the tool name the model sees: 1 to 64 letters, digits, _ or -. Each value holds the tool options; "operation" is required and names the Kirak operation to run. Python function tools are registered in code, not here.

x-kirak-errors.pattern: a tool key must be a name the model sees: 1 to 64 letters, digits, _ or -, e.g. "orders_fetch" or "refund".

fixed.query: query Orders($status: String) { orders(status: $status) { id total } }

operation.description: The Kirak operation to run: "<model>.<crud_op>", "<module>.<op>", or "graphql".

description.description: What the tool does and when to use it, written for the model. Default: the model's or the module operation's own description.

requires_confirmation.description: A human approves each call before it runs. Default: derived from the operation effect (write/destructive -> true, read -> false).

fixed.description: Values the model cannot change. Removed from the model's visible input schema and merged into the call at runtime.

params.description: JSON Schema constraints added on top of the parameters the model still fills. A key must not appear in both fixed and params.

enum.description: The only values the model may pass.

pattern.description: Regular expression a string must match.

format.description: JSON Schema format of a string, e.g. "email" or "date-time".

output.description: MCP server files: JSON Schema of the result's data, for operations whose result depends on the provider (payments, notifications, storage, ...). It becomes the tool's outputSchema, and every result is checked against it: one that does not match is an OUTPUT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH error. Best with fixed.provider, so one provider's shape comes back. Agent files ignore it.
